text:
maya: heads-up — rolled CNI 1.24.0 to west2 canary (3 nodes) ~10:12 UTC, seeing east-west packet loss between GPU pods and RDMA handshake timeouts, training jobs stalling
owen: ack — symptoms? retries / error messages?
maya: intermittent 0.5-1.5% pkt loss, all-reduce stalls, dmesg shows RDMA failures and netwatchdog timeouts
maya: logs:
```
[rdma] mlx5_0: rdma: handshake failed status=-110
kernel: NETDEV WATCHDOG: eth0 tx_timeout
```
owen: can you grab conntrack counters and ethtool offload state from one of the affected nodes? `conntrack -S` + `ethtool -k eth0`
lia: we didn't touch MTU, but tunnel/encap counters spiked during the rollout on those nodes (saw fragmentation increase)
infra-bot: deploy: cni/1.24.0 -> west2-canary completed (3/3) at 10:15 UTC
maya: starting rollback on the 3 canary nodes now — reverting to 1.23.4 to validate
owen: +1 for rollback, also run a quick iperf3 between two GPU pods to confirm baseline before/after
maya: ran `iperf3 -c` between pods: before rollback ~ 950 Mbps, after rollout ~ 520-700 Mbps (sporadic dips)
lia: note — affected nodes are on older NIC firmware and we had SR-IOV enabled on them. Could be offload/encap interaction with the new tunneling code path
sre-oncall: moving thread to #incidents and paging kernel/net team — cc @netops @kernel-eng :rotating_light:
owen: once rollback is done, please capture `ip link show`, `bridge fdb show`, and `ethtool -S` for the node — we need to see if encap fragmentation counters correlate
maya: rollback finished at 10:28 UTC, packet loss dropped back to baseline and RDMA handshake errors cleared :thumbsup:
owen: good. next steps: create an upgrade checklist that includes RDMA smoke tests + SR-IOV verification and NIC firmware compatibility check
lia: we should also add a pre-rollout probe: small all-reduce job + iperf3 and an MTU fragmentation probe across all AZs (catch fragmentation before full rollout)
sre-oncall: filing incident ticket with timeline, canary node ids, and captured logs — will attach to the ticket and schedule follow-up retro
maya: summary: CNI 1.24.0 introduced an encap/tunnel path change that interacts poorly with SR-IOV + older NIC firmware -> causes RDMA handshake timeouts and transient packet loss on GPU pods. Rollback to 1.23.4 restored stability.
owen: agreed — prioritize test automation + firmware gating before next canary. Thanks all.
